requirement: Provide pytest marker factories that skip a test unless every named environment variable is set and non-empty, or unless an executable is found on PATH, each with a reason naming exactly what is missing.
skeleton: requires_env validating that names were given, collecting unset or empty variables and returning pytest.mark.skipif with a reason, and requires_tool returning skipif based on shutil.which.
caption: Reusable pytest skip conditions built as marker factories on pytest.mark.skipif, using the standard-library os and shutil modules. requires_env(*names) raises ValueError asking to name at least one environment variable when called with none. Each time it is called it reads os.environ, treating a variable that is unset or set to an empty string as missing, and returns pytest.mark.skipif whose condition is whether anything is missing and whose reason is missing environment followed by the missing names in the order given, so a decorated test is skipped with a precise explanation instead of failing on absent configuration. requires_tool(tool) asks shutil.which whether an executable of that name exists on PATH, which ignores files without the executable bit, and returns pytest.mark.skipif that skips when the tool is not found with the reason tool not found on PATH. Both return a pytest.MarkDecorator whose mark exposes name, args and kwargs. The fixture asserts that two present variables give a skipif mark with condition False, that DB_USER and DB_PASS missing give condition True and the reason naming both, that an empty variable counts as missing, that the environment is read at call time, that no names raises ValueError, that an executable on a patched PATH does not skip, and that a non-executable file of the same name skips with the PATH reason.

plan.intent: Skip integration tests cleanly when their prerequisites are absent
constraints: Calling requires_env with no names raises ValueError
Unset and empty variables both count as missing and are named in the reason
The environment is read when the marker is built
Tools are found with shutil.which so non-executable files do not count

rationale.teaches: Returning pytest.mark.skipif with a computed condition and reason from a helper, and inspecting a MarkDecorator's mark in tests.
rationale.why: Presence checks that accept empty values or plain file existence skip nothing on a broken machine, and an inverted condition or wrong marker type turns skips into silent passes or expected failures.

ops.docstring: Build skipif markers for tests that need environment variables or tools.

candidates.why_wrong: A variable set to an empty string counts as present, so the test runs without usable configuration.
The condition is inverted, so tests skip when configured and run when variables are missing.
Checking file existence ignores the executable bit and treats PATH as a single directory.
With no names nothing is missing, so the marker never skips and hides the mistake.
xfail still runs the test and reports it as an expected failure instead of skipping it.
